newsitem.title: POLAND: Polish, Ukrainian premiers work for freer border.
newsitem.headline: Polish, Ukrainian premiers work for freer border.

text.p: Ukraine's Prime Minister Pavlo Lazarenko, starting a two-day visit to Poland, on Monday oversaw the clinching of deals aimed at promoting cross-border transport and customs cooperation to boost economic links.

The neighbours have increasingly stressed their strategic partnership, with Ukraine accepting Poland's goal of joining NATO and Warsaw acting as advocate in Western and Central Europe for Ukraine's foreign policy goals.
Lazarenko and his Polish counterpart Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz confirmed this relationship was on track.
"Our talks today...confirmed that Poland for Ukraine and Ukraine for Poland are very important strategic partners," Cimoszewicz said after a meeting at his Warsaw offices.
"We are grateful to our Ukrainian friends for their full understanding of Poland's aspirations," he told reporters.
The main emphasis of Lazarenko's visit, which is accompanied by a session of a mixed commission on economic affairs, fell on promoting trade and border cooperation.

Ministers and senior officials signed deals agreeing on the location, near Poland's Korczowa, where the new Polish A4 motorway will link up with a similar Ukrainian highway and on joint maintenance of bridges at the border.
They also agreed that customs and border officials would cooperate in jointly checking people, parcels and vehicles at one of the congested crossings between the two countries.
The deal is part of a process aimed at freeing traffic across the border, crossed millions of times each year by people seeking to shop and trade.
Last year Warsaw and Kiev agreed on visa-free travel for their citizens, which awaits the settlement of final details before taking effect.
Lazarenko said the two countries would also approach the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development for funding to further improve border customs posts.

He said Poland would offer government guarantees for credits to expand production of Polish Bizon tractors in Kovel in Ukraine and the two would also discuss production of farm machinery in Kharkov as well as the possibility of Polish-Ukrainian-Italian cooperation in food processing.
Both agreed that current trade levels were unsatisfactory and they should do everything to improve them, Lazarenko said.
In 1996 Poland's exports to Ukraine totalled $742.6 million compared with imports from there of $290.8 million, figures cited by Poland's foreign ministry show.

On Tuesday the Ukrainian prime minister was due to meet Poland's President Aleksander Kwasniewski, who is set to visit Ukraine in May and sign a declaration of reconciliation dealing with some difficult chapters in Polish-Ukrainian history.
